name: PinkPantheress
label: Warner Records
lede: She posted a song a day because she had nothing else to do, and four years later a mixtape with a crown on the cover landed among the best albums of 2025.

eras.title: A song a day, nothing else to do
eras.text: A university student in Kent posts loops on TikTok, two go viral, and two labels sign her within months. The mixtape follows.

years.cap: PinkPantheress performing at Le Poisson Rouge in 2022 · Wikimedia
years.h: Day 11 of posting a song every day: [[PinkPantheress|7441014f-f8f5-494f-81db-ff166fbc078d]] and "Pain"
years.p: A student in Kent recorded one song an hour after class and posted 20-second loops to TikTok. The 12-second "Pain" clip caught fire.
years.xp:
Victoria Walker, then studying film at University of the Arts London, posted the "Pain" snippet in January 2021 with the caption "Day 11 of posting a song every day bc i have nothing else to do." It built on a sample of Sweet Female Attitude's 2000 garage hit "Flowers" and a piano loop based on Erik Satie's "Trois Gymnopédies".

She made it herself, and it runs 1:38. The full song came out on June 7, 2021, peaked at No. 35 in the UK and later went platinum there; Pitchfork ranked it No. 90 on its 2024 list of the 100 best songs of the 2020s so far.

years.h: Parlophone in April, Elektra in June
years.p: Two labels signed the TikTok bedroom producer within about two months of each other.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists her deals as Parlophone in April 2021 and Elektra Records in June 2021. Her first mixtape came out on both labels that October.

years.h: "Just for Me": a four-hour session with [[Mura Masa|d2a76e1b-cecc-4500-b445-d55591821cd3]]
years.p: The song about an unhealthy crush hit No. 27 in the UK and got two million TikTok videos.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, PinkPantheress cited Eminem's "Stan" and a wish to sound like Craig David as starting points. Mura Masa produced, played drums and keyboards, and the pair cut it in a four-hour studio session about two weeks before release.

[[Central Cee|b0337af1-8d93-4671-b6c9-ba306bf942bf]] later sampled it heavily for "Obsessed with You", and Giveon and Coldplay both covered it for BBC Live Lounge.

years.h: To Hell with It: 18 minutes 36 seconds, one mansion, one lightning bolt
years.p: The debut mixtape packed jungle, UK garage and pop-punk onto a short runtime and debuted at No. 20 in the UK.
years.xp:
It samples Sweet Female Attitude, Crystal Waters' "Gypsy Woman" and Linkin Park's "Forgotten". Producers include Mura Masa, Adam F and Oscar Scheller. Pitchfork gave it 7.3, calling her vocals strangely soothing; Metacritic lists it at 86.

The cover, shot by Brent McKeever, has her outside a mansion at night with lightning behind her.

eras.title: Sound of 2022, and a quieter ear
eras.text: The BBC crowns her, and a hearing problem forces her off a festival bill.

years.h: BBC picks her for Sound of 2022
years.p: She won the poll of tastemakers before she had released a proper record beyond a handful of singles and the mixtape.

years.h: She pulls out of Primavera Sound over hearing loss
years.p: Wikipedia says she became about 80% deaf in her right ear in 2022 after microphone feedback.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, voices sound to her mostly like bass. She cancelled her scheduled Primavera Sound Barcelona set that June, citing hearing loss.

eras.title: Boy's a Liar, and a first album
eras.text: A remix with Ice Spice makes her a transatlantic pop name, and Heaven Knows follows.

years.cap: PinkPantheress performing at Brooklyn Paramount in 2024 · Wikimedia
years.h: "Boy's a Liar Pt. 2" with [[Ice Spice|6f2c949d-9540-4421-bf02-27ae27e00e33]] goes to No. 3
years.p: It debuted at No. 14 on the Billboard Hot 100, then rose to No. 3, the first top ten for both artists.
years.xp:
Ice Spice had posted her own version on Instagram; PinkPantheress reached out with the idea of "stamping" the song into 2023 and rebuilt it from Mura Masa's instrumental stems. The video, by George and Frederick Buford, was shot in mid-January 2023 around New York, including Harlem rooftops, fire escapes and subway cars.

It peaked at No. 2 in Canada and No. 1 in New Zealand, and went platinum in the US. Several outlets called its absence from the 2024 Grammy nominations a snub.

years.h: Heaven Knows: the first album, and the split verdict
years.p: Central Cee, Rema and Kelela guest, and Mura Masa and Greg Kurstin produce. Pitchfork gave it 6.4; Clash gave it 9.
years.xp: It peaked at No. 28 in the UK and No. 61 on the Billboard 200, and Metacritic sits at 80 from 15 critics. Rolling Stone ranked it No. 64 on its best albums of 2023. Singles were "Boy's a Liar Pt. 2", "Mosquito", "Capable of Love" and "Nice to Meet You" with [[Central Cee|b0337af1-8d93-4671-b6c9-ba306bf942bf]].

eras.title: The pause
eras.text: She tours behind Olivia Rodrigo, then pulls the rest of her dates for health reasons.

years.h: She cancels the rest of the year's shows
years.p: After opening on Olivia Rodrigo's Guts tour, she pulled remaining August dates and cited health reasons.

eras.title: Fancy That
eras.text: A mixtape of big-beat, jungle and garage pop lands on year-end lists, and the awards follow.

years.h: "Tonight" samples Panic! at the Disco strings
years.p: The lead single for Fancy That lifts the orchestral strings from "Do You Know What I'm Seeing?" and got a Regency costume video.
years.xp:
Brendon Urie, Ryan Ross, Spencer Smith and Jon Walker get writing credits for the 2008 Panic! at the Disco original. Aksel Arvid and Count Baldor produced with PinkPantheress. Director Charlotte Rutherford took cues from Bridgerton and Jamiroquai's "King for a Day".

It reached No. 35 in the UK. Slant named it the best song of 2025, per Wikipedia.

years.h: "Stateside" borrows from Adina Howard and Groove Armada
years.p: She called it her favorite song on Fancy That; it went to No. 3 in the UK.
years.xp: It samples Adina Howard's 1995 "Freak like Me" and Groove Armada's 1999 "I See You Baby". Aksel Arvid, Harrison Patrick Smith, Jkarri and PinkPantheress produced. The [[Zara Larsson|134e6410-6954-45d1-bd4a-0f2d2ad5471d]] remix, released October 10, hit No. 6 on the Hot 100 and topped the Billboard Global 200.

years.cap: PinkPantheress in the Imperial State Crown
years.src: Wikipedia: Fancy That · Metacritic: Fancy That critic reviews
years.h: Fancy That: garage, jungle and a crown
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.0 and ranked it No. 18 of 2025. It debuted at No. 3 in the UK, her highest-charting album at home.
years.xp:
Harry Tafoya's Pitchfork review scored it 8.0; Metacritic lists it at 82 from 11 critics, all positive, with Variety at 92 and DIY at 100. It leans on Basement Jaxx, Groove Armada and Fatboy Slim, and 11,126 first-week UK units got it to No. 3.

She described the cover, with her in the Imperial State Crown among flowers, as everything kitsch and UK-centric. It also placed No. 7 on Billboard's year-end list.

years.h: "Illegal" flips Underworld and takes over TikTok
years.p: The single samples "Dark & Long (Dark Train)" and spawned a handshake trend; it reached No. 22 in the UK.
years.xp: She called it garage that is "gritty" and "takes me right back to where I started with music." Ethan & Tom directed the video. It became her second Hot 100 entry at No. 96.

years.p: Kylie Minogue, Sugababes, Seventeen, Anitta, Bladee and Basement Jaxx remix or join. Pitchfork gave it 7.6.
years.xp: Disc three reissues the original mixtape whole. The project reached No. 30 on the Billboard 200 and No. 1 on Top Dance Albums. Pitchfork asked who else would have the cheek to gather all these people under one roof.

years.h: Two Grammy nominations for the Fancy That era
years.p: "Illegal" for Best Dance Pop Recording, and Fancy That for Best Dance/Electronic Album.

years.h: She wins Brit for British Producer of the Year
years.p: She became the youngest winner and the first woman to take the award.
